newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe industry opposes CSCE coffee contract cut.
newsitem.headline: Europe industry opposes CSCE coffee contract cut.

text.p: The European Coffee Federation (ECF) said in a letter to the New York Coffee, Sugar & Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) that it opposed a planned cut in the size of the arabica futures contract.
The letter, made available to Reuters by German coffee industry association DKV, said the proposal, first made in April, envisaged halving the trading unit of the "C" contract from 250 to 125 bags.
ECF secretary general Roland Vaessen said the move would create substantial additional costs for futures users because commission had to be paid per transaction.
At the same time, it was doubtful whether the proposal could help increase liquidity and open interest in an attempt to reduce price volatility.
Vaessen said, "We subscribe to the intended purpose of this change...however, we have strong reservations whether the proposed measure adequately addresses the root cause of the problem."
The ECF believed the CSCE needed to address a different set of problems.
The contract limited the delivery basis to washed arabicas and so excluded a large volume of coffee.
The increased emphasis on broker activities discouraged green coffee buyers from actively operating on the futures market, the ECF said.
The export-marketing policy of producer countries created a structure in the "C" contract that discouraged the trade to participate actively in futures.
And it was impossibe to deliver coffee spot Europe.
The plan appeared likely to benefit financial interests, funds and floor brokers, who were less concerned than genuine hedgers with maintaining a solid link with the cash market.
The Brussels-based ECF is the umbrella organisation of the European green coffee trade and roasting industry.
It is made up of national coffee associations in 13 European countries and represents an import volume of around 36 million bags a year.
